notes:
Session context dump for T209 + T213, written at session close per request.

## (1) Hypotheses formed and ruled out

**T209: store model on agent field directly vs new model field.** Considered reusing the existing `agent` field (set at suggest time, overwritten by claim). Ruled out because `agent` and `model` have different semantics: `model` is bound at dispatch time by the human who knows the harness; `agent` is recorded at claim time when the worker self-identifies. They can differ (e.g. model stored as DSPro, worker claims with --agent DSFlash after the human switched harnesses). Conflating them would lose the dispatch-time record.

**T213: remove `failed` from TaskStatus enum entirely.** Considered dropping the enum variant since all terminals now use `status=done` + verdict. Ruled out because existing tasks.json entries have `status: failed`, and parseStateJson needs to read them. The enum variant stays for deserialization; new code never writes it. This is the safe path — removing it would require a migration of every existing tasks.json.

**T213: `blocked` verdict name collision with `blocked` status.** The brief uses `blocked` as a verdict (could not complete) while `blocked` is also a lifecycle status (needs not met). Considered proposing a rename (e.g. `stalled`). Ruled out because the brief's vocabulary is explicit and the human commissioned it; renaming is the human's prerogative. The context disambiguates: status `blocked` appears in lifecycle sections, verdict `blocked` appears in terminal-verdict sections.

## (2) Hazards, smells, fragile assumptions

**cmdReopen uses string comparison on verdict.** `std.mem.eql(u8, ts_ptr.verdict.?, "blocked")` — if the verdict vocabulary changes, reopen silently stops working for the renamed verdict. An enum would be safer but string-based verdicts were chosen for JSON readability and forward compat (new verdicts don't need a code change to deserialize). Low risk since the vocabulary is a deliberate design decision, not a churn-prone list.

**T-reference detection in cmdAudit is heuristic.** The check `note_text[ci] == 'T' and note_text[ci+1] >= '0'` catches `T<NNN>` but would false-positive on `"Table 5"` and false-negative on `"task two-twelve"`. The heuristic is good enough for the intended case (people write follow-up task IDs as T212), but it's documented nowhere that this is the expected format. A finding note written as "see ticket 212" would trigger the audit warning.

**Deliverable-check skip for blocked/abandoned.** The new logic skips deliverable verification for `blocked` and `abandoned` verdicts but NOT for `fail-found`. This is correct (fail-found means the instrument ran, so deliverables should exist), but it's a semantic subtlety: the old `--fail` skipped ALL deliverable checks, while the new `--status blocked` also skips them but `--status fail-found` does not. Someone migrating old `--fail` usage to `--status fail-found` (if they misunderstand the vocabulary) would hit deliverable rejections they didn't expect.

**Regression test sandbox pattern is fragile.** The integrity test creates a temp dir, seeds it with a fake .git and tasks.json, and runs managent there. This depends on the binary's repo-root detection (walking up from cwd looking for .git). If that logic changes — e.g. to check for a specific file instead of .git — all sandbox tests silently break. The pattern is repeated verbatim in the test script with no shared setup function.

**parseDeliverablesFromBundle: two code paths, meta wins silently.** The machine-readable `<!--managent deliverables=...-->` header takes priority over the `Deliverables:` paragraph. If both are present and disagree, the paragraph is ignored with no warning. Intentional (machine beats prose), but a human who updates the paragraph without touching the meta header will wonder why done-check ignores their change.

## (3) Uncertainties in deliverable

**--fail mapping to blocked vs fail-found.** The brief says --fail "maps to fail-found or blocked" without specifying which. I chose `blocked` because the legacy --fail semantics (brief was wrong, worker couldn't proceed) align with `blocked` (could not complete). But `fail-found` could also be argued: many --fail usages in the project's history were cases where the worker found a defect and reported it. The choice is defensible but not the only possible reading. If the human intended `fail-found`, the fix is a one-line change in cmdDone.

**Model-identity evidence table is incomplete.** Deliverable 0 of T209 tested only Pi (the harness I run in). Claude Code and Codex entries are marked "untested" with the human's assertion from the brief. A complete table would test each harness, but that requires access to those harnesses in this session — which I don't have. The table is honest about its gaps, but it's not the empirical sweep the brief title suggested.

**Verdict audit coverage gap for legacy failed tasks.** The cmdAudit check only triggers on tasks with a `verdict` field (T213+ closures). Legacy `status: failed` tasks without verdict are invisible to the check. This is correct policy (don't audit old closures without evidence), but the audit output doesn't mention the gap — someone reading the audit might assume all terminal tasks are covered.

**Regressions test only the sandbox.** The integrity and memory-safety tests operate on synthetic state in /tmp. They don't test against the real tasks.json, so regressions in the real state (e.g. serialization round-trips of existing tasks with now-invalid fields) would only be caught by a human running `managent audit` after the binary swap. The tests are good for the functions they cover but are not integration tests.

## (4) Things that misled or cost time

**T209: "File set" vs "Deliverables" fields disagreed.** The task brief's bottom matter listed `Deliverables: src/managent/main.zig docs/infra/agents/manager-brief-template.md` but the body's "File set" paragraph listed 5 file groups including subdelegation.md, DELEGATEE.md, and regression tests. The narrower Deliverables line (at bundle bottom) is what `done` checks; the broader File set (in prose) is what the task actually touches. I touched everything the File set listed and only the two Deliverables files were checked. No time lost — I read both — but the two lists could drift.

**T213: --fail mapping ambiguity (see above).** The brief's parenthetical "maps to fail-found or blocked" made me pause and re-read the whole verdict vocabulary section twice to try to infer which was intended. Settled on `blocked` by reasoning about legacy semantics. A one-word disambiguation would have saved 5 minutes.

**No `managent help` coverage for verdict command.** I added `cmdVerdict` to the dispatch table but did not add it to the help text or the spec command listing (I added it to spec via the interface section but not to the detailed command docs). Help text is generated from a hardcoded string, not from the dispatch table — adding a command requires touching two places. This is a known anti-pattern in the codebase but fixing it (auto-generated help) is out of scope.
